info.description: If blocked requests (SQL Injection, XSS, etc.) from WAF exceed the set threshold, the IP will be automatically blocked. Blocked IPs can be managed in the WAF/Ban IP tab.

trustedIps.title: Global Trusted IPs
trustedIps.description: IPs that bypass per-host perimeter controls (geo restriction, access lists, bot filter, rate limiting) and are never automatically banned (Fail2ban, WAF Auto-Ban, IP bans). By default they do NOT bypass WAF rules or exploit/scanner blocking, but the option below lets you also bypass the WAF (ModSecurity).
trustedIps.help: Add internal network ranges, monitoring systems, or trusted service IPs. These addresses bypass per-host perimeter controls (geo restriction, access lists, bot filter, rate limiting), are excluded from automatic banning (Fail2ban, WAF Auto-Ban), and are removed from the banned IP list in nginx configs. By default they still pass through WAF rules and exploit/scanner detection, so a compromised trusted host cannot proxy attacks to the backend. If needed, the option below also disables WAF (ModSecurity) inspection for these IPs. Supports IPv4, IPv6, and CIDR notation.
trustedIps.format: One IP or CIDR per line. Lines starting with # are comments. Supports IPv4, IPv6, and CIDR. Invalid entries are silently ignored.

bypassWaf.label: Trusted IPs also bypass the WAF (ModSecurity)
bypassWaf.description: When enabled, requests from the trusted IPs above skip ModSecurity / OWASP CRS WAF inspection entirely. Off by default.
bypassWaf.help: Advanced option. When enabled, the ModSecurity rule engine is turned off for all requests from the trusted IPs above (the full WAF is skipped). Use this only when legitimate traffic from a trusted host is being blocked by WAF false positives. It does not affect nginx-level rules such as exploit/scanner blocking (block_exploits) or the bot filter.
bypassWaf.warning: WAF protection is fully disabled for these IPs. Only add addresses you truly trust — if such a host is compromised, attacks can reach your backend without WAF inspection.

global.title: Global Settings
global.description: Manage Nginx global settings. Nginx will automatically reload after saving changes.

buttons.resetConfirm: Reset all global settings to defaults?

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Standard balanced configuration. Suitable for most cases.

performance.label: Performance
performance.description: High performance configuration. Optimized for high traffic and fast responses.

security.label: Security
security.description: Security hardened configuration. Uses only modern TLS and adds security headers.

buffer.title: Proxy Buffer Settings
buffer.description: Configure how responses from upstream servers are buffered. Proper buffer sizing balances memory usage and performance.

performance.tips: Tip: If proxy buffer size is too small, responses will be written to temporary files, causing disk I/O. Increasing buffer size improves performance for large responses. Open File Cache caches file descriptors for static files to improve performance.

worker_processes.label: Worker Processes
worker_processes.description: Number of worker processes handling requests. 0 = auto-detect based on CPU cores. Higher values improve concurrency.

worker_connections.label: Worker Connections
worker_connections.description: Maximum number of simultaneous connections per worker process. Higher values allow more concurrent connections.

multi_accept.label: Multi Accept
multi_accept.description: If enabled, a worker will accept all new connections at once. Improves performance under high traffic.

use_epoll.label: Use Epoll
use_epoll.description: Use efficient event processing method (epoll) on Linux. Improves performance with many concurrent connections.

keepalive_timeout.label: Keepalive Timeout (s)
keepalive_timeout.description: Time to keep connections alive. Allows clients to reuse connections for multiple requests.

keepalive_requests.label: Keepalive Requests
keepalive_requests.description: Maximum number of requests that can be served through a single keepalive connection.

client_max_body_size.label: Max Body Size
client_max_body_size.description: Maximum allowed size of the client request body (e.g., 100m, 1g). Affects file upload limits.

types_hash_max_size.label: Types Hash Size
types_hash_max_size.description: Maximum size of the MIME types hash table. Default is usually sufficient.

sendfile.label: Sendfile
sendfile.description: Use sendfile() system call to transfer files directly in the kernel. Improves static file serving speed.

tcp_nopush.label: TCP Nopush
tcp_nopush.description: Use in conjunction with sendfile. Sends response header and file content in one packet.

tcp_nodelay.label: TCP Nodelay
tcp_nodelay.description: Disable Nagle algorithm. Sends small packets immediately. Useful for real-time applications.

server_tokens.label: Server Tokens
server_tokens.description: If enabled, Nginx version is shown in response headers. Recommended to disable for security.

gzip_enabled.label: Gzip Compression
gzip_enabled.description: Compress responses with Gzip. Saves bandwidth and improves page load speed.

gzip_comp_level.label: Compression Level (1-9)
gzip_comp_level.description: Compression strength. Higher means better compression but more CPU usage. Recommended: 5-6.

gzip_min_length.label: Min Compression Length (bytes)
gzip_min_length.description: Responses smaller than this will not be compressed. Compressing tiny files can be inefficient.

gzip_types.label: Compression MIME Types
gzip_types.description: List of MIME types to compress. Effective for text-based content (HTML, CSS, JS, JSON, etc.).

gzip_vary.label: Add Vary Header
gzip_vary.description: Adds 'Vary: Accept-Encoding' header. Ensures CDNs/caches serve the correct version.

brotli_enabled.label: Brotli Compression
brotli_enabled.description: Enable Brotli compression. Provides higher compression ratio than Gzip. Supported by modern browsers.

brotli_static.label: Brotli Static
brotli_static.description: Serve pre-compressed .br files if available. Reduces CPU overhead for static assets.

brotli_comp_level.label: Brotli Level (1-11)
brotli_comp_level.description: Brotli compression strength. 1-4: Fast, 5-9: Balanced, 10-11: Max (High CPU). Recommended: 4-6.

brotli_min_length.label: Brotli Min Length
brotli_min_length.description: Minimum response size (bytes) to apply Brotli compression. Small files don't benefit from compression.

brotli_types.label: Brotli MIME Types
brotli_types.description: List of MIME types to compress with Brotli. Most effective for text-based content.

ssl_protocols.label: SSL Protocols
ssl_protocols.description: Allowed TLS protocol versions. TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3 are recommended for security.

ssl_ciphers.label: SSL Ciphers
ssl_ciphers.description: List of enabled cipher suites. Balance between security and compatibility.

ssl_ecdh_curve.label: ECDH Curves
ssl_ecdh_curve.description: Elliptic curve groups for key exchange. Include X25519MLKEM768 for post-quantum (ML-KEM) TLS support with modern browsers.

ssl_session_cache.label: SSL Session Cache
ssl_session_cache.description: Cache SSL sessions to speed up reconnects by skipping handshake.

ssl_session_timeout.label: SSL Session Timeout
ssl_session_timeout.description: Validity period of SSL session cache. e.g., 1d (1 day), 1h (1 hour).

ssl_prefer_server_ciphers.label: Prefer Server Ciphers
ssl_prefer_server_ciphers.description: Use server's preferred cipher suites instead of client's. Recommended for stronger security.

ssl_stapling.label: OCSP Stapling
ssl_stapling.description: Cache certificate status on server to speed up client connection verification.

ssl_stapling_verify.label: Stapling Verify
ssl_stapling_verify.description: Verify OCSP response. Used with ssl_stapling.

ssl_session_tickets.label: Session Tickets
ssl_session_tickets.description: Enable TLS session tickets for session resumption. Reduces server load.

client_body_timeout.label: Client Body Timeout (s)
client_body_timeout.description: Timeout for reading client request body. Adjust for slow uploads.

client_header_timeout.label: Client Header Timeout (s)
client_header_timeout.description: Timeout for reading client request header. Protects against slow clients.

send_timeout.label: Send Timeout (s)
send_timeout.description: Timeout for transmitting response to client.

proxy_connect_timeout.label: Proxy Connect Timeout (s)
proxy_connect_timeout.description: Timeout for connecting to upstream server.

proxy_send_timeout.label: Proxy Send Timeout (s)
proxy_send_timeout.description: Timeout for sending request to upstream server.

proxy_read_timeout.label: Proxy Read Timeout (s)
proxy_read_timeout.description: Timeout for reading response from upstream server. Adjust for slow API responses.

resolver.label: DNS Resolver
resolver.description: DNS server for resolving domain names. e.g., 8.8.8.8 8.8.4.4 valid=300s

error_log_level.label: Error Log Level
error_log_level.description: Logging verbosity. 'debug' is most detailed, 'crit' is most concise.

access_log_enabled.label: Enable Access Log
access_log_enabled.description: Log all requests. High traffic may increase disk usage.

custom_http_config.label: Custom HTTP Config
custom_http_config.description: Directly input additional Nginx configuration. For advanced users.

proxy_buffer_size.label: Proxy Buffer Size
proxy_buffer_size.description: Buffer size for reading the first part (header) of upstream server response. Default: 8k

proxy_buffers.label: Proxy Buffers
proxy_buffers.description: Number and size of response buffers. Format: 'count size' (e.g., 8 32k)

proxy_busy_buffers_size.label: Busy Buffers Size
proxy_busy_buffers_size.description: Buffer size that can be sent to client while response is not fully read.

proxy_max_temp_file_size.label: Max Temp File Size
proxy_max_temp_file_size.description: Maximum size of temporary file for storing response when buffers are full. Set to 0 to disable temp files.

proxy_temp_file_write_size.label: Temp File Write Size
proxy_temp_file_write_size.description: Size of data that can be written to temporary file at once.

proxy_buffering.label: Proxy Buffering
proxy_buffering.description: When on, nginx buffers the entire response before sending to client. Turn off for large downloads or real-time streaming.

proxy_request_buffering.label: Proxy Request Buffering
proxy_request_buffering.description: When on, nginx buffers the entire request body to disk before forwarding. Turn off to stream uploads directly without creating temp files.

open_file_cache_enabled.label: Enable Open File Cache
open_file_cache_enabled.description: Cache open file descriptors and directory lookups. Improves performance for sites with many static files.

open_file_cache_max.label: Max Cache Entries
open_file_cache_max.description: Maximum number of entries to keep in cache.

open_file_cache_inactive.label: Inactive Time
open_file_cache_inactive.description: Entries not accessed within this time are removed from cache. (e.g., 20s, 60s)

open_file_cache_valid.label: Validation Interval
open_file_cache_valid.description: How often to check if cached entries are still valid. (e.g., 30s, 60s)

open_file_cache_min_uses.label: Minimum Uses
open_file_cache_min_uses.description: Only files accessed this many times are kept in cache.

open_file_cache_errors.label: Cache Errors
open_file_cache_errors.description: Also cache file-not-found errors. Improves performance for repeated requests to non-existent files.

reset_timedout_connection.label: Reset Timedout Connections
reset_timedout_connection.description: Close timed out connections with RST instead of FIN to immediately release sockets. Helps conserve server resources.

resolver_timeout.label: DNS Resolver Timeout
resolver_timeout.description: Maximum time to wait for DNS lookup response. (e.g., 30s)

custom_stream_config.label: Custom Stream Config

cloudflareTunnel.title: Cloudflare Tunnel
cloudflareTunnel.description: Expose your proxy hosts through a Cloudflare Tunnel — no port forwarding required.
cloudflareTunnel.enableDescription: When enabled, the built-in cloudflared connector establishes an outbound connection to Cloudflare. No need to open ports 80/443 on your router.
cloudflareTunnel.tokenDescription: The tunnel connector token issued in the Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard. It is shown masked after saving.
cloudflareTunnel.tokenPasteHint: Paste the full install command — the token is extracted automatically.

guide.title: Setup Guide
guide.step1: In the Cloudflare Zero Trust dashboard, go to Networks → Tunnels → Create a tunnel and create a tunnel using the Cloudflared connector.
guide.step2: Copy the connector token shown after creating the tunnel — it is the <TOKEN> part of the 'cloudflared service install <TOKEN>' install command.
guide.step3: Paste the token into the field above, enable the tunnel, and save.
guide.step4: Add a Public Hostname to the tunnel with a wildcard per domain (e.g. *.example.com), point the service to {{originUrl}}, and turn ON "No TLS Verify" in the TLS settings.
guide.redirectLoopWarning: Pointing the service to http://localhost:80 causes redirect loops on hosts with Force HTTPS enabled. Always use {{originUrl}}.
guide.wildcardPriorityWarning: Cloudflare matches Public Hostnames top-to-bottom (first match wins). A single wildcard (*.example.com) is enough — NPG routes each request to the right proxy host by its Host header. If you also add specific hostnames, place them ABOVE the wildcard, or the wildcard will shadow them and send traffic to the wrong origin.
guide.httpOnlyNote: For a proxy host served over plain HTTP (SSL disabled), point that hostname's service to {{originUrlHttp}} instead — the https origin above is for SSL-enabled hosts.
guide.step5: (Optional) Clean up old A records and router port-forwarding rules for the domains you moved to the tunnel.

cloudflareTunnel.enable: Cloudflare Tunnel only uses an outbound connection from your server to Cloudflare, so proxy hosts can be exposed without port forwarding or opening your firewall. It can take up to a minute after enabling for the connection to come up.
cloudflareTunnel.token: The connector token issued when you create a tunnel in Cloudflare Zero Trust. It is stored only on the server and shown masked (first 4 characters) after saving. Click Replace to store a new token.

global.worker_processes: Number of Nginx worker processes. Set to 'auto' to match CPU cores. Matching core count is recommended for high traffic.
global.worker_connections: Max simultaneous connections per worker. Too low values can cause connection errors. (Default: 1024)
global.multi_accept: If enabled, workers accept multiple connections at once. Can improve performance under very high traffic.
global.use_epoll: Uses epoll, a high-performance event processing method on Linux. Essential for handling many concurrent connections.
global.keepalive_timeout: Time to keep connection alive. Too long wastes memory, too short causes reconnection overhead.
global.keepalive_requests: Max requests per keepalive connection. Connection closes after exceeding this limit.
global.client_max_body_size: Limits max upload file size. Increase this if you need to upload large files.
global.types_hash_max_size: Size of hash table for MIME types. Default is usually sufficient.
global.sendfile: Maximizes performance by transferring files at kernel level. Essential for static content.
global.tcp_nopush: Used with sendfile to reduce packet count and improve network efficiency.
global.tcp_nodelay: Sends small packets immediately to improve response speed. Beneficial for real-time apps.
global.server_tokens: Hiding Nginx version information is recommended for security.
global.gzip_enabled: Compresses text data (HTML, CSS, JS) to reduce transfer size. Greatly improves speed.
global.gzip_comp_level: Compression level. 5-6 offers best balance between CPU usage and efficiency.
global.gzip_min_length: Very small files are not compressed as it offers no benefit.
global.gzip_types: File types to compress. Images/videos are already compressed so better to exclude them.
global.gzip_vary: Adds Vary header so cache servers distinguish compressed vs uncompressed versions.
global.brotli_enabled: Uses Google's Brotli compression. Higher compression ratio than Gzip.
global.brotli_types: Content types to compress with Brotli.
global.ssl_protocols: Avoid using old protocols (SSLv3, TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1) as they have security vulnerabilities.
global.ssl_ciphers: List of encryption algorithms. Keep updated for strong security.
global.ssl_ecdh_curve: Key exchange curve groups. X25519MLKEM768 enables post-quantum TLS for modern browsers (Chrome, Edge, Safari).
global.ssl_session_cache: Caches SSL handshake info to speed up reconnections.
global.ssl_session_timeout: Duration to keep SSL session cache.
global.ssl_prefer_server_ciphers: Prioritize server's cipher suite preference over client's.
global.ssl_stapling: Speeds up certificate validation to reduce connection latency.
global.ssl_session_tickets: Resumes SSL sessions quickly using session tickets.
global.client_body_timeout: Closes connection if client sends data too slowly.
global.client_header_timeout: Closes connection if client sends headers too slowly.
global.send_timeout: Timeout for sending data to client.
global.proxy_connect_timeout: Timeout for connecting to backend server.
global.proxy_send_timeout: Timeout for sending data to backend server.
global.proxy_read_timeout: Time to wait for response from backend. Increase if you have slow API endpoints.
global.resolver: DNS server used to resolve domain names to IPs.
global.error_log_level: Detail level of error logs. 'warn' or 'error' recommended unless debugging.
global.access_log_enabled: Logs all access records. May require disk space management.
global.custom_http_config: Enter custom configuration to add to Nginx http block.
global.proxy_buffer_size: Buffer size for reading the first part (header) of upstream server response.
global.proxy_buffers: Number and size of buffers for buffering responses. Format: 'count size'
global.proxy_busy_buffers_size: Buffer size for sending partial response to client while upstream is still sending.
global.proxy_max_temp_file_size: Maximum size of temp file for storing response when buffers are full. Set to 0 to disable temp files.
global.proxy_temp_file_write_size: Size of data written to temp file at once.
global.proxy_buffering: When on, nginx buffers the entire upstream response before sending to client. Turn off for SSE, large downloads, or real-time streaming to avoid temp files.
global.proxy_request_buffering: When on, nginx buffers the entire request body to disk before forwarding to upstream. Turn off to stream uploads directly without creating temp files. Recommended for large file uploads (10GB+).
global.open_file_cache_enabled: Cache file descriptors and metadata for static files. Improves performance for sites with many static files.
global.open_file_cache_max: Maximum number of entries to store in cache.
global.open_file_cache_inactive: Cache entries not accessed within this time are removed.
global.open_file_cache_valid: How often to check if cached entries are still valid.
global.open_file_cache_min_uses: Only files accessed this many times within inactive time are kept in cache.
global.open_file_cache_errors: Also cache file-not-found and similar errors.
global.reset_timedout_connection: Close timed out connections with RST packet. Quickly frees socket resources to improve server performance.
global.resolver_timeout: Maximum time to wait for DNS lookup response.
global.custom_stream_config: Nginx stream block configuration for TCP/UDP load balancing.

ddos.connectionLimit: Limits concurrent connections from same IP to protect server resources.
ddos.requestLimit: Limits requests per second from same IP to block excessive requests.
ddos.responseLimit: Limits download speed to prevent bandwidth monopoly.
ddos.bandwidthLimit: Limits client download speed to fairly distribute bandwidth.

geoip.enable: Enabling GeoIP allows you to block or allow traffic based on country. Requires a free MaxMind account.
geoip.account: You need a MaxMind Account ID and License Key to download the GeoLite2 database.
geoip.accountId: The 6-digit ID issued from your MaxMind account settings.
geoip.licenseKey: The license key generated from your MaxMind account.
geoip.updateInterval: Frequency to automatically update the GeoIP database.

acme.enable: Automatically issues and renews free SSL certificates from Let's Encrypt.
acme.email: Used for certificate expiration notifications and account recovery.
acme.staging: Use Staging for testing to avoid rate limits. Certificates are NOT trusted. Disable for production.
acme.renewBefore: Renew certificates this many days before expiration. Default (30) is recommended.

botfilter.defaults: These settings apply as defaults for NEW Proxy Hosts only. Existing hosts are unaffected.
botfilter.badBots: Blocks known bad bots like scrapers and spammers.
botfilter.aiBots: Blocks AI data scrapers like GPTBot and ClaudeBot.
botfilter.searchEngines: Always allow search engine crawlers (Google, Bing) to protect SEO.
botfilter.suspicious: Challenges suspicious clients (curl, python-requests) with a JavaScript challenge.

waf.autoBan: Automatically bans IPs that generate frequent WAF alerts (e.g., SQL Injection) within a short time.
waf.threshold: Ban IP if detection count exceeds this number within the window.
waf.duration: Duration to ban the IP. 0 means permanent ban.

maintenance.logRetention: Older logs are automatically deleted to save disk space. (Runs daily at midnight or on system restart)
maintenance.rawLogs: Save raw Nginx access/error logs to disk for external analysis or compliance.
maintenance.access: All HTTP request records including Bot Filter and Exploit block events. Used for traffic analysis.
maintenance.stats: Retention period for dashboard charts and statistics.

backup.enable: Automatically backup entire configuration at scheduled times.
backup.schedule: Backup schedule in Cron format (e.g., 0 2 * * * = Daily at 2 AM).
backup.retention: Maximum number of backup files to keep. Oldest backups are deleted when exceeded.

roles.title: Roles
roles.subtitle: Grant read/write permissions per menu area and assign roles to users.
roles.name: Role name
roles.builtinHint: Built-in roles cannot be edited. Duplicate one if you need something similar.
roles.superuserHint: The administrator role reaches every area, including areas added in future releases.
roles.deleteBlocked: {{count}} user(s) still hold this role. Move them to another role first.

users.title: Users
users.subtitle: Create admin panel accounts and assign roles.
users.cannotDeleteSelf: You cannot delete your own account
users.passwordHint: At least 10 characters with upper and lower case, a digit and a symbol. A change is required on first login.
users.resetHint: Resetting ends every session of that account and requires a change on next login.
users.deleteTokenWarning: {{count}} API token(s) issued by this user are deleted with it and stop working immediately.
users.effectiveHint: What the account actually reaches, not the role’s stored rows.

sso.title: SSO (OpenID Connect)
sso.subtitle: Sign in to the admin panel with a standard OIDC provider — Google, Authentik, Authelia, Keycloak and others.
sso.empty: No providers yet. Adding one puts a button on the login screen.
sso.callbackHint: Register this exact value at the provider. A single character of difference fails the sign-in.
sso.localLoginNote: Password sign-in always stays available. NPG is often the reverse proxy in front of the very provider you configure, so an SSO-only panel would lock you out of the tool you need to fix it.
sso.provisioningHint: Authenticated is not authorized. A public provider such as Google authenticates every account on earth, so automatic creation only turns on once you say who is allowed.
sso.jitNeedsAllowlist: Set an allowed domain, an allowed email, or a required group first.
sso.mappingsAuthoritative: With mappings set, the role is recomputed at every sign-in — removing a group at the provider takes effect on the next login.
sso.mappingsNone: With no mappings, the role is set once when the account is created and NPG owns it from then on.
sso.deleteBody: Delete '{{name}}'. Its {{count}} linked account(s) are unlinked, not deleted.

fields.name: Display name
fields.slugHint: Used in the URL. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
fields.issuerHint: The provider's discovery base, e.g. https://accounts.google.com
fields.secretKeepHint: Leave unchanged to keep the stored secret.
fields.callbackBaseHint: Pins the public origin when NPG sits behind another proxy. Derived from the request when empty.
fields.requiredGroupHint: When set, only members of this group may sign in.
fields.allowJit: Create an account the first time someone signs in
fields.defaultRoleHint: The role a newly created account receives

steps.access: Who may sign in, and as what?

presets.googleHint: Fixed for every Google account — leave it exactly as it is, with no trailing slash.
presets.authentikHint: https://<your-authentik-domain>/application/o/<application-slug>/ — the slug is the one authentik fills in when you create the application.
presets.autheliaHint: The root URL you reach Authelia on — scheme and host only, no path, no trailing slash.
presets.keycloakHint: https://<keycloak-host>/realms/<realm-name> — the realm URL itself, not the discovery path.
presets.genericHint: The provider's discovery base — everything before /.well-known/openid-configuration

sso.testPkceUnknown: The provider does not advertise PKCE support. It usually still works.
sso.testMissingScopes: Scopes the provider does not advertise: {{scopes}} — it may still work, but check.
sso.testFailed: Could not connect. Check the address and that NPG can reach it.
sso.groupsScopeMissing: Group rules are set but the requested scopes do not include `groups`. Most providers withhold group information without it, so every sign-in would be refused as not permitted.

steps: In the Google Cloud Console, pick or create a project to hold the client.
Register the app and set Audience to External if anyone signs in with a personal Gmail account, or Internal if everyone is in your Workspace organisation.
Create a client with Application type set to Web application — that is the type that issues a client secret.
Add {{callback}} to Authorized redirect URIs. Google matches it exactly and rejects plain http, bare IP addresses and wildcards.
Copy the client ID and secret straight into the fields below: Google shows the full secret only once, though you can rotate it later.
If your Audience is External and the app is still in Testing, add each person to the Test users list or Google will block them.
google.groups: Google sends no group information over OIDC, so assign roles per account here. To limit sign-in to one Workspace organisation, set Audience to Internal rather than looking for a groups setting.
google.requires: Before you start: this panel must be reachable on a real domain over https, and Google cannot assign roles by group — you set each account's role here.

steps: In authentik, open Applications → Applications and create a new application, which sets up its provider in the same pass.
Note the Slug authentik fills in — it appears in the issuer URL above.
Choose OAuth2/OIDC as the provider type and leave Client Type on Confidential so a client secret is generated.
Under Redirect URIs, add {{callback}} with mode set to Strict.
Set a Signing Key, such as the built-in self-signed certificate — leaving it empty breaks token signing.
Create it, then reopen the provider to copy the Client ID and Client Secret.
authentik.groups: authentik's default profile scope already emits a groups claim, so leaving the group claim name as "groups" is enough — no custom mapping needed.

steps: Authelia has no admin interface — open configuration.yml and find or create identity_providers.oidc.
Generate a client ID and a hashed secret with the authelia crypto commands, and keep the plaintext secret for the field below.
Add the client under identity_providers.oidc.clients and leave `public` unset so it stays confidential.
Keep scopes as openid, profile, email and groups, and add {{callback}} as the redirect URI.
On Authelia 4.39 and newer, add a claims policy that puts email, preferred_username and groups in the ID token — otherwise they are only returned from the UserInfo endpoint.
Restart Authelia; it does not reload its configuration on its own.
authelia.groups: groups is already in Authelia's default scopes. On 4.39 and newer the claims policy is what actually places it in the ID token, which is where NPG reads it.

steps: Switch to the realm your users actually log in to — a client in the master realm cannot authenticate them.
Create a client with Client type set to OpenID Connect.
Turn Client authentication On. It is off by default, which produces a public client with no secret for NPG to use.
Set Valid redirect URIs to exactly {{callback}}, with no wildcard, and save.
Open the client's Credentials tab and copy the Client secret into the field below.
keycloak.groups: Keycloak sends no group information until you add it: on the client's dedicated scope, add a Group Membership mapper, set Token Claim Name to groups and turn Full group path off.

sso.googleCallbackHttp: Google will refuse this callback URL: it accepts only https (localhost excepted). Reach this panel on a real domain with a valid certificate before setting Google up.
sso.googleCallbackIP: Google will refuse this callback URL: it does not accept IP addresses. Reach this panel on a real domain name with a valid certificate before setting Google up.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.subtitle: Send security events and a daily summary to Discord, Telegram or a webhook — ntfy, Gotify, Home Assistant and the like.
notifications.quietByDesign: Quiet by design. An ongoing failure is announced when it starts and when it recovers, not in between, and bursts such as IP bans are coalesced into a single message.
notifications.empty: No channels yet. Add one and notifications will start arriving there.
notifications.failing: {{count}} consecutive failures — the channel turns itself off at 10
notifications.deleteBody: Delete '{{name}}'. Notifications routed here will stop.
notifications.whatToSendHint: For each alert: off, delivered the moment it happens, or mentioned only in the daily summary. Once the channel is saved you can preview any of them.
notifications.piiNote: Request headers, cookies, user-agent, request URL and raw log data are deliberately unavailable: they carry credentials, and a notification leaves your network.

fields.name: Name
fields.webhookUrlHint: The address your ntfy, Gotify, Apprise or Home Assistant instance gave you
fields.discordUrlHint: Channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks. The URL is itself the credential.
fields.botTokenHint: Create a bot with @BotFather and it hands you one.
fields.chatIdHint: Bots cannot start a conversation. Message the bot or add it to your group first, then find the chat id.
fields.authHeaderHint: Only if your receiver requires one, e.g. Bearer tk_xxx
fields.allowPrivateHint: Turn this on only to reach an ntfy or Gotify on your own network. By default NPG will not send to a private address or a container name.
fields.templateHint: Leave empty for the default format.
fields.secretKeepHint: Leave unchanged to keep the stored value.

richFormatHint.discord: Sends an embed with a title, a severity-coloured bar and the fields as columns. Off sends one plain block.
richFormatHint.telegram: Sends MarkdownV2 with a bold title and highlighted values. Off sends plain text.
richFormatHint.webhook: The JSON body is always structured; this only affects the human-readable text line.

fields.languageHint: The language of alerts sent to this channel, chosen per channel and independent of the panel's own language.
fields.dashboardUrlHint: Appended to the daily summary as a link. Use the address the people reading this channel actually reach the panel on. Empty means no link.
fields.payloadFormatHint: Choose plain text for receivers whose URL carries the topic, like ntfy — send them JSON and the phone shows raw JSON. Gotify, Apprise, Home Assistant and your own receivers want JSON.
fields.digestHourZoneMismatch: This server runs on {{server}} while your browser is on {{browser}}, so the two clocks differ — enter the hour in the server’s time, not your local time. (Set TZ in your docker compose file to change what the server uses.)

webhook.title: At your receiver
steps: Create a receiving address in whatever will show the notification — ntfy, Gotify, Apprise, Home Assistant.
Paste it into Receiver URL below. If the receiver needs authentication, put the token in the Authorization header field.
Save, then press Send test and confirm it actually arrives.

discord.title: In Discord
steps: In the channel that should receive alerts: Edit Channel → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook.
Press Copy Webhook URL. That URL is itself the credential — anyone holding it can post to the channel.
Paste it into Discord webhook URL below, save, and press Send test.

telegram.title: In Telegram
steps: Message @BotFather and send /newbot. Give it a name and a username, and it hands you a bot token that looks like 123456:ABC-DEF. Paste that below.

A bot cannot message you first. To receive privately, open the chat with your new bot and send it anything. To receive in a group, add the bot to the group and send a message there. To receive in a channel, add the bot as a channel admin and post once.
Press Detect chat id below and NPG lists the conversations the bot can see. Click the one you want and the chat id fills in.
Save, then press Send test — a real message should arrive.

notifications.detectEmpty: The bot can see no conversations yet. Message it directly, add it to a group and post there, or add it as a channel admin and post once — then try again.
notifications.detectPick: Pick the conversation to send to:

cert.renewal_failed.label: Certificate renewal failed
cert.renewal_failed.desc: A Let's Encrypt renewal failed. Left alone the certificate expires and the site stops loading.

cert.renewed.label: Certificate renewed
cert.renewed.desc: Sent only when a renewal that had been failing works again.

ddns.sync_failed.label: DDNS update failed
ddns.sync_failed.desc: Your public IP changed but DNS was not updated, so you may lose access from outside.

ddns.recovered.label: DDNS updating again
ddns.recovered.desc: Sent only when a failing DDNS record starts working again.

backup.failed.label: Scheduled backup failed
backup.failed.desc: The automatic backup did not run. You have no new restore point.

nginx.reload_failed.label: nginx reload failed
nginx.reload_failed.desc: Applying the config failed through every retry. nginx keeps serving the old config, so changes such as IP bans are not in effect.

auth.login_failed.label: Admin sign-in locked out
auth.login_failed.desc: Failed sign-ins hit the lockout threshold. Often a brute-force attempt.

ip.banned.label: IP banned
ip.banned.desc: fail2ban or WAF auto-ban blocked an address. These arrive in bursts, so they are coalesced every five minutes.

sso.login_refused.label: SSO sign-in refused
sso.login_refused.desc: An identity outside your allowlist tried to sign in — a misconfiguration, or somebody trying.

notifications.testThisEvent: Send this exact alert now so you can see how it looks

payloadFormats.json: JSON (Gotify, Apprise, Home Assistant, your own receiver)

errors.invalid_name: Enter a name between 1 and 64 characters.
errors.invalid_url: That receiver URL is not valid. It must start with http:// or https://, and sending to a private network address needs "Allow a private receiver" turned on.
errors.invalid_bot_token: Enter the bot token — the "digits:letters" string @BotFather gave you.
errors.invalid_chat_id: Enter the chat ID. Message the bot, or add it to a group or channel and post once, then press Detect chat id to fill it in.
errors.invalid_events: Pick at least one alert, or turn on the daily summary.
errors.invalid_event: That includes an alert this version does not know. Reload the page and try again.
errors.invalid_dashboard_url: The dashboard address must start with http:// or https://.
errors.invalid_digest_hour: The send hour must be between 0 and 23.
errors.invalid_language: The message language must be Korean or English.
errors.invalid_config: A setting has leading or trailing whitespace — remove the spaces that came along when pasting.
